summary: The team is in the final push for the CKGSB-IE 'China Going-Global' report launch tomorrow, while simultaneously advancing the Intelligent China and Asia Start programs and resolving a lingering Outlook account lockout.
summaryDetail: The most urgent priority is the CKGSB-IE report launch on September 15: the webpage must be shared by Ira, Xuan, and Julie, the press release needs final edits from Felix and Ira, and Joseph must update the page with edited copy—all today. In parallel, the Intelligent China program is gaining momentum with the webpage launch, email campaigns, and rewritten copy awaiting sign-off from Cao Yi and Jay, while the Emerging Tech Management Week page rewrite is under review by Alan, Renee, and Xin. The Asia Start program remains a strategic focus for SEO and marketing, with Joseph drafting target areas and the team analyzing participant profiles. This week also requires finalizing alumni confirmations and registrant approvals for the September 14 luncheon, and ensuring the BCI/BSI indices are featured on the knowledge homepage. The Outlook account lockout, though less strategic, still needs resolution across all devices and backend confirmation from JSB to prevent further disruption.

meetings.title: Outlook Account Password Reset & Device Check
meetings.summary: The team troubleshoots an Outlook account lockout caused by stale saved passwords on multiple devices, resetting the password and re-logging in across laptops and phones. They also briefly discuss a meeting summarization tool and a class-related matter.

meetings.title: Knowledge Website Design Review
meetings.summary: The team reviewed the proposed knowledge website design, noting it is similar to the current site except for improved menu categorization. They discussed incorporating elements from Joseph's editorial-style inspiration and agreed on next steps for feedback.

meetings.title: CKGSB Global Marketing Strategy Meeting
meetings.summary: The team discussed prioritizing China-based programs (Asia Star and Intelligent China) for SEO and marketing, with a focus on AI, EVs, and smart manufacturing. They also reviewed conversion tracking setup and planned next steps for audits and content optimization.

decisions.text: Remove the videos panel and integrate videos into topics instead of having a separate category.
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge and School) at the top.
Use Joseph's design as inspiration but not follow it exactly; combine ideas with the current version.
Bring BCI and BSI indices to the knowledge homepage.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for marketing efforts.
Put US partnership programs (Stanford, Berkeley, Columbia) on hold initially, but consider Berkeley as a third priority.
Focus on China-based programs due to higher demand from overseas executives.
Keep Dean Xiang's keynote speech to 10 minutes from 12:35–12:45 PM, followed by Ira's report presentation
